title: Bihu
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
info: Bihu dance, with dhol and pepa
body:
Bihu is a set of three important cultural festivals in Assam, marking the agricultural cycle and the Assamese New Year.

The three Bihus

Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu, April) is the Assamese New Year and the most celebrated — with Bihu dance, songs, feasts and new clothes. Kongali Bihu (Kati Bihu, October) is quieter, marked by lighting lamps in paddy fields. Bhogali Bihu (Magh Bihu, January) is the harvest festival, famous for its community feasts, bonfires (meji) and traditional food.
extra:
Bihu dance and music

Bihu dance is performed in groups, with quick steps, hip movements and hand gestures, to the beat of the dhol, the sound of the pepa (buffalo-horn pipe) and the gagana. Traditional dress includes the mekhela chador for women and the dhoti and gamosa for men.

Food

Bihu feasts feature pitha (rice cakes), laru (sweet balls), fish, duck and pork dishes, and rice beer in some communities. Bhogali Bihu in particular is a festival of eating together.
